Active ingredient technology

Acephate 75% SP — organophosphate chemistry

Acephate (IRAC Group 1B) is a proven organophosphate insecticide that inhibits acetylcholinesterase in insect nerve tissue, causing feeding disruption and nervous-system impact. This widely trusted chemistry delivers effective pest control against thrips, aphids, whiteflies, jassids, bollworms, and allied sucking and chewing pests across Indian farming systems.

Systemic action — absorbed by plant tissues

Acephate absorbs through foliage and translocates via xylem, protecting new shoots and unsprayed plant parts from inside out. Systemic movement ensures long-lasting activity against newly active pests between spray intervals, making HIL THENE a true systemic insecticide for dependable crop protection in cotton, chilli, paddy, tomato, brinjal, okra, and vegetable programs.

Contact action — quick pest knockdown

Acephate delivers rapid contact kill on pests directly exposed to the spray deposit. Thrips, whiteflies, aphids, and jassids experience immediate feeding cessation and nervous-system disruption — providing fast pest suppression when applied at economic threshold with thorough leaf surface and underside coverage at 25 gm per pump.

How does ACEPHATE 75% SP work?

Systemic organophosphate mode of action — ACEPHATE 75% SP delivers contact activity, feeding inhibition, nervous-system disruption, and long residual protection inside plant tissue.

  1. 1

    SP dissolution and foliar deposit

    On application, HIL THENE dissolves rapidly in water and forms an even spray deposit on leaf surfaces. Pests contact or ingest treated foliage, absorbing Acephate through cuticle and gut.

  2. 2

    Contact action — rapid knockdown

    Acephate acts on contact, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase in insect nerve tissue. Thrips, whiteflies, aphids, and jassids exposed to the spray deposit experience rapid nervous-system disruption and immediate cessation of feeding damage.

  3. 3

    Systemic absorption — Acephate

    Acephate (IRAC Group 1B) is absorbed through foliage and translocates via xylem, protecting new shoots and unsprayed plant parts from inside out — a proven organophosphate insecticide mechanism.

  4. 4

    Feeding disruption

    Acephate disrupts normal nerve signalling through acetylcholinesterase inhibition, causing continuous stimulation that stops pest feeding soon after exposure — limiting crop damage even before full mortality occurs.

  5. 5

    Nervous system impact

    The organophosphate mode of action causes paralysis and death in target sucking and chewing pests, delivering fast action and long-lasting suppression of thrips, aphid, whitefly, and bollworm populations.

  6. 6

    Long residual field protection

    Systemic acephate activity within plant tissue maintains protection against newly active pests between scheduled spray intervals, supporting sustainable crop protection programs.

ACEPHATE 75% SP mode of action

How Acephate in HIL THENE delivers contact, systemic, and translaminar action for comprehensive thrips, aphid, whitefly, and bollworm control.

Contact action — rapid knockdown

Acephate acts on contact, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase in insect nerve tissue. Thrips, whiteflies, aphids, and jassids exposed to the spray deposit experience rapid nervous-system disruption and immediate cessation of feeding.

Systemic activity

When pests ingest treated plant tissue, acephate delivers strong systemic insecticide activity against hidden feeders on leaf undersides and in dense canopy — protecting the entire crop from inside out.

Feeding disruption

Acephate disrupts normal nerve signalling through acetylcholinesterase inhibition. Susceptible pests lose the ability to feed and move normally — a powerful organophosphate insecticide mechanism.

Long residual protection

Systemic acephate activity within plant tissue maintains protection against newly active pests between spray intervals. Rotate HIL THENE with neonicotinoids, IGRs, and other MOA groups across the season.

Application method

Step-by-step guide for applying HIL THENE (ACEPHATE 75% SP) in the field.

Step 1 — Prepare clean water

Half-fill a standard 15-litre knapsack sprayer with clean water before adding the insecticide for safe, even mixing.

Step 2 — Measure 25 gm

Accurately measure 25 gm of HIL THENE for one knapsack pump. Use a graduated measure for consistent dosing.

Step 3 — Mix thoroughly

Add product to water, top up the tank, and agitate. The SP formulation suspends easily into a uniform spray mix.

Step 4 — Spray uniformly

Apply in calm weather. Cover both leaf surfaces and undersides where thrips, whiteflies, aphids, and jassids feed.

Storage instructions

Store HIL THENE in the original sealed container in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place away from direct sunlight, food, feed, seed, and children. Keep containers upright and locked. Do not store near heat sources or open flames. Shelf life is approximately 24 months from date of manufacture when stored properly. Triple-rinse empty bottles before disposal as per local pesticide container management rules.

Usage best practices

Mix clean, spray calm, scout again after a few days.

  • 1

    Wear proper PPE

    Always wear gloves, protective clothing, goggles, and a fitted mask when handling concentrate or preparing the spray mix.

  • 2

    Accurate 25 gm dose

    Measure exactly 25 gm per pump to maintain efficacy, protect crops, and slow resistance development in thrips, aphid, and whitefly populations.

  • 3

    Avoid spray drift

    Apply in calm weather, avoid spraying near water bodies, and keep children, animals, and beehives away from the application zone.

Storage, disposal & first aid

Respect the label hazard panel and local disposal rules.

  • 4

    Safe storage

    Store in original sealed container in a cool, dry, locked place away from direct sunlight, moisture, food, feed, seed, and children.

  • 5

    Container disposal

    Triple-rinse empty packs, puncture them, and dispose as per local pesticide container management rules.

  • 6

    First aid readiness

    If product contacts skin or eyes, wash thoroughly with water. If swallowed or symptoms appear, seek medical help immediately with the label.

Compatibility & tank mix

HIL THENE is generally compatible with commonly used insecticides and fungicides when tank-mixed for integrated crop protection programs. Always perform a jar test before mixing to confirm physical compatibility. Avoid alkaline mixes that may degrade active ingredients. Consult your local Harishree dealer or agronomist for crop-specific tank-mix recommendations.

Resistance management

ACEPHATE 75% SP chemistry in HIL THENE supports focused thrips, whitefly, and aphid management when rotated with other mode-of-action groups. For sustainable sucking pest control, rotate HIL THENE with organophosphates, IGRs, and other insecticide classes across the season and avoid repeated applications of the same chemistry alone.

Expert recommendation

Agricultural advisors recommend HIL THENE when fields show thrips, whitefly, or aphid pressure — particularly chilli thrips, cotton whitefly, vegetable aphids, jassids, or mixed sucking pest complexes on cotton, chilli, and vegetables. Apply at early infestation or economic threshold with 25 gm per pump and thorough leaf underside coverage for best results. Integrate HIL THENE into a broader integrated pest management program with scouting, ETL-based decisions, and rotation across MOA groups for long-term sustainable sucking pest management.

Frequently asked questions

Practical answers about ACEPHATE 75% SP, HIL THENE, dose, uses, and safe field use.

Acephate 75% SP is a soluble powder insecticide containing Acephate (IRAC Group 1B organophosphate) at 75% concentration for broad-spectrum control of thrips, aphids, whiteflies, jassids, bollworms, leafhoppers, and other sucking and chewing pests on cotton, chilli, paddy, tomato, brinjal, okra, and vegetable crops.

HIL THENE is Harishree Crop Science's brand of Acephate 75% SP — a systemic and contact organophosphate insecticide for thrips control, aphid control, whitefly control, jassid control, and bollworm control in Indian cotton, chilli, paddy, and vegetable programs. Recommended dose: 25 gm per pump.

HIL THENE controls thrips, aphids, whiteflies, jassids, bollworms, leafhoppers, leaf-eating caterpillars, and other sucking and chewing pests when applied at early infestation with thorough leaf surface and underside coverage.

Yes. HIL THENE (Acephate 75% SP) is highly effective against chilli thrips and vegetable thrips when sprayed at economic threshold with emphasis on flowers, pods, and leaf undersides where thrips feed and reproduce.

Yes. HIL THENE controls both aphids and whiteflies through systemic and contact acephate activity. Apply at early colonization on cotton and vegetables for aphids and whiteflies at 25 gm per pump.

The standard recommended dose of HIL THENE is 25 gm per pump in a 15-litre knapsack sprayer filled with clean water. Always confirm the final dose with the printed label and local agronomic advisory.

Acephate 75% SP (HIL THENE) is widely used on cotton for jassid and bollworm control, on chilli for thrips control, on paddy for hopper and borer management, and on vegetables including tomato, brinjal, and okra at 25 gm per pump.

Fill a 15-litre knapsack sprayer with clean water, add 25 gm of HIL THENE, mix thoroughly until the SP dissolves, and spray uniformly over foliage with emphasis on leaf undersides. Apply in calm morning or evening hours for best thrips, aphid, and whitefly control.
